record.paper_title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations: numerical results for the heat semigroup and open questions on them (with appendix: full list of pictures and Python code)
record.context_brief: Linear dependence on low Hölder exponent
record.original_question: For the heat equation u_t(t,x)=u_xx(t,x) on the real line, work in the Banach space UC_b(R) of bounded uniformly continuous real functions with the sup norm. Let Lf=f'' generate the heat semigroup e^{tL}. For t=1/2, compare the exact solution e^{tL}u0 with Chernoff products G(t/n)^n u0 and S(t/n)^n u0, where G is first-order Chernoff tangent to L and S is second-order Chernoff tangent to L. Write d_n^G=||e^{tL}u0-G(t/n)^n u0|| and d_n^S=||e^{tL}u0-S(t/n)^n u0||, and estimate log d_n approximately as alpha log n plus beta, where alpha is the order of decreasing error and beta is the free term. For the low-regularity families u0(x)=|sin x|^xi and u0(x)=exp(-|x|^xi), where xi is the Hölder or smoothness exponent and 0<xi<1, why do both estimated orders alpha_G and alpha_S appear to depend linearly on xi? Is there a theorem predicting this linear dependence, and what constants or structural features determine the slopes for the trigonometric and exponential families?

Paul Chernoff’s theorem [3] implies that for eacht >0, eachu 0 ∈ Fsequences dG n =∥e tLu0 −G(t/n) nu0∥, d S n =∥e tLu0 −S(t/n) nu0∥ converge to 0 asn→ ∞, but it saysnothingabout the rate of convergence.
For all of them, we numerically calculated lnd G n ≈α G lnn+β G,lnd S n ≈α S lnn+β S. We callαthe order of decreasing error,βthe free term of decreasing error.
We use the letterξto denote the smoothness class of the initial condition. We use lettersα S andβ S for the Chernoff functionS, andα G andβ G for the Chernoff functionG.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the heat equation u_t(t,x) = u_{xx}(t,x) for (t,x) ∈ [0,∞) × ℝ on the Banach space F = UC_b(ℝ) of bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions on ℝ with the sup norm ‖f‖ = sup_{x∈ℝ}|f(x)|. The operator L f = f'' generates the heat C_0-semigroup (e^{tL})_{t≥0} on F.

Define two families of bounded linear operators on F by

  (G(t)f)(x) = (1/2) f(x) + (1/4) f(x + 2√t) + (1/4) f(x − 2√t),
  (S(t)f)(x) = (2/3) f(x) + (1/6) f(x + √(6t)) + (1/6) f(x − √(6t)),

so that G is Chernoff-tangent to L of first order and S is Chernoff-tangent to L of second order. By Chernoff's theorem, for every t > 0 and every u_0 ∈ F,

  d_n^G(t,u_0) := ‖e^{tL} u_0 − G(t/n)^n u_0‖ → 0,
  d_n^S(t,u_0) := ‖e^{tL} u_0 − S(t/n)^n u_0‖ → 0 as n → ∞.

Fix t = 1/2 and, for each parameter ξ ∈ (0,1), consider the two families of initial data

  u_0^{(sin)}(x) = |sin x|^ξ,    u_0^{(exp)}(x) = exp(−|x|^ξ),

both of which lie in F and belong to the Hölder class of exponent ξ. Empirically one finds a power-law decay

  log d_n^G ≈ α_G(ξ) log n + β_G(ξ),   log d_n^S ≈ α_S(ξ) log n + β_S(ξ),

and α_G(ξ) and α_S(ξ) each appear to be linear functions of ξ on (0,1) for both families.

Problem. Prove (or disprove) that for these two families of low-regularity initial conditions, the orders of decrease α_G(ξ) and α_S(ξ) of the Chernoff approximation error depend linearly on the Hölder/smoothness exponent ξ ∈ (0,1), and identify the slopes and intercepts of these linear dependences in terms of the structure of the Chernoff functions G and S and of the initial-data family (trigonometric |sin x|^ξ versus exponential exp(−|x|^ξ)). In particular, provide a theorem that predicts the observed linear dependence and explains why the slopes differ between the trigonometric and exponential families.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a numerical/empirical observation seeking a theoretical explanation; recent literature on Chernoff-approximation convergence rates (e.g. upper/lower estimates in the Chernoff product formula, Israel J. Math. 2024; convergence-rate results for Hölder initial data for convex monotone semigroups, 2025) provides general Hölder-type bounds but no source found explicitly proves the conjectured linear dependence of α_G(ξ) and α_S(ξ) on the smoothness exponent ξ for these specific |sin x|^ξ and exp(−|x|^ξ) families. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Upper and lower estimates for rate of convergence in the Chernoff product formula for semigroups of operators
status_evidence.snippet: Provides general upper and lower estimates for Chernoff product convergence rates, but not the specific linear-in-ξ behavior for the families considered.
status_evidence.claim: General theory gives bounds but does not directly settle the linear dependence on ξ.

status_evidence.title: Convergence rates for Chernoff-type approximations of convex monotone semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit convergence rates for Chernoff-type approximations when initial data are Hölder continuous.
status_evidence.claim: Hölder-class rates have been studied, but not in the specific empirical-slope form asked here.

status_evidence.title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical observation of approximately linear dependence of α on ξ, posed as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The linear dependence is observed numerically and posed as an open theoretical question.
